title: Majestic Knight
transcript: Both players are about to get a new queen, but if white tries to now run to promotion, black is actually faster. He's going to get a queen on the next move. And once white does the same and promotes to his own queen, well, now unfortunately black is actually going to be able to capture that queen. So, this is going to be a win for black, but there doesn't seem to be any way to stop this promotion. The white knight is simply too far away, but as it turns out, that is just an illusion. The white knight is perfectly on time to stop the black pawn. How, you might wonder? With the brilliant knight [music] to E4. A beautiful sacrifice, preparing to meet the promotion to the queen with this fork of the king and queen, forcing the king to move and picking up the queen, meaning that white would win this game. But, of course, black doesn't have to promote right away. He's still faster than white, so he can just take this knight and then promote on the next move. But, sometimes chess can be quite ironic. And in this situation, black actually gets a taste of his own medicine, because after he gets the new queen and white promotes, too, this time there is going to be a black king in the way. This is a check. The king has to move, meaning that white will now be the one able to capture the black queen, turning the tables and winning the game. If you like this board, read the caption.
